name: Freelance Work Document (Wathiqat Al-Amal Al-Hur)

requirement_groups.name: Saudi national or Premium Residency holder

requirements.blocker_text: The Freelance Work Document is issued by HRSD only to Saudi nationals and to Premium Residency (Iqama Mumtaza) holders -- it is NOT available to ordinary expatriates on a standard employer-sponsored Iqama, regardless of profession.
requirements.fix_path: Obtain Premium Residency first (see sa_premium_residency_investor_entrepreneur or sa_premium_residency_talent_gifted) -- there is no other route to this document for a foreign national.

requirements.blocker_text: The applicant's profession must fall within HRSD's approved freelance-activity list (over 120 professions as of mid-2026, spanning IT, marketing, consulting, creative services, and some licensed professions), set and periodically updated by HRSD.
requirements.fix_path: Confirm the specific activity is on the current HRSD-approved freelance profession list at freelance.sa before applying.

requirements.blocker_text: Applicants must be at least 18 years old.
Applicants must be no older than 60 years old.

evidence_required.document: National ID (Saudi nationals) or Premium Residency card
Registration via the Unified National Access (Nafath) and Absher biometric verification
Proof of practice or qualification in the selected profession category

outcome.duration_length: 1 year, free renewal via the platform before expiry

sources.title: Ministry of Human Resources and Social Development (hrsd.gov.sa) -- Freelance Work Document issuance and renewal service
Ministry of Human Resources and Social Development -- Al-Amal Al-Hur (Freelance Work) programme description, confirming Saudi-national eligibility base

notes: LIVE DISCREPANCY CAUGHT, and a genuinely important one: multiple English-language 2026-dated 'expat guide' sites (SafariStar, Gulf Corporate Services, gulfwisdom.com) describe this as a general-purpose freelance visa open to any foreign national with a standard Iqama -- a materially misleading claim that could lead an applicant to waste real time and money pursuing an application they don't qualify for. The official HRSD Arabic-language service page and a directly-quoted third-party platform reproducing HRSD's own stated conditions ('يجب أن يكون المتقدم لإصدار الوثيقة من المواطنين السعوديين' -- the applicant must be a Saudi national) both confirm the base eligibility is Saudi nationality, with a 2026-dated update extending it specifically to Premium Residency holders as a named exception -- not to expatriates generally. This is the same category of live catch as the UK/Germany/Netherlands salary-threshold discrepancies documented elsewhere in this dataset, except here the error is categorical (who qualifies at all) rather than numeric. fw_status is modeled as an OR-list against current_route_held including 'saudi_national' as a value -- a genuine edge case for this schema, since Mapply's routes are designed for foreign applicants and 'already being a citizen' isn't normally a relevant attribute value; included here because the fix_path correctly routes a foreign applicant toward Premium Residency as the only real path into this document, which is itself valuable product information even though the route's primary qualifying condition isn't something a foreign applicant starts with. switchable_to is empty because holding this document doesn't itself lead anywhere further in the route graph -- it's a standing work-authorisation status, not a step toward settlement.
